# massdriver Provider

The Massdriver provider manages two distinct surfaces:

- **Platform resources** (projects, environments, components, component links, instance alarms, groups, group policies, OCI repositories, imported resources) — the design-time topology of an organization on Massdriver. These are typically managed from CI/CD or a local workstation by a platform team.
- **Deployment-context resources** (`massdriver_resource`) — provisioned resources declared by a bundle's `massdriver.yaml`, produced at deploy time from inside the bundle's IaC.

The two surfaces have different authentication requirements. Pick the credentials that match the context where the terraform will run.

## Example Usage

Most setups need nothing more than an empty provider block — the provider reads its configuration from `MASSDRIVER_*` environment variables:

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    massdriver = {
      source  = "massdriver-cloud/massdriver"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "massdriver" {}
```

### Platform operations

For terraform running from CI/CD or a workstation managing platform resources, the simplest setup is to export an API key and your organization ID before running `terraform apply`:

```shell
export MASSDRIVER_API_KEY="mds_..."
export MASSDRIVER_ORGANIZATION_ID="your-org-id"

# Optional — only when targeting a self-hosted instance:
# export MASSDRIVER_URL="https://api.massdriver.example.com"
```

The same values can be set directly in the provider block (HCL takes precedence over env vars). Prefer variables over literals so credentials don't end up in source control:

```terraform
variable "massdriver_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

provider "massdriver" {
  api_key         = var.massdriver_api_key
  organization_id = "your-org-id"
  # url = "https://api.massdriver.example.com" # self-hosted only
}
```

### Bundle deployments

When the terraform runs inside a Massdriver bundle deployment, **no configuration is required**. The platform injects `MASSDRIVER_DEPLOYMENT_ID` and `MASSDRIVER_TOKEN` into the deployment environment automatically; the empty `provider "massdriver" {}` block above just works.

This is by design: a bundle's IaC ships an empty provider block once, and the same HCL runs in every deployment without changes. Deployment-token auth has no HCL knobs — the platform owns those credentials.

## Authentication

The provider reads credentials from standard `MASSDRIVER_*` environment variables resolved by the [Go SDK](https://github.com/massdriver-cloud/massdriver-sdk-go). Two methods are supported.

### API key auth

For platform-management terraform running from CI/CD or a workstation.

| Env var | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MASSDRIVER_API_KEY` | yes | Either a service account token or a personal access token. |
| `MASSDRIVER_ORGANIZATION_ID` | yes | The Massdriver organization ID. |
| `MASSDRIVER_URL` | no | API base URL. Defaults to Massdriver's managed SaaS platform; override when targeting a self-hosted instance. |

### Deployment token auth

Injected automatically by Massdriver into a bundle's IaC at deploy time. You generally don't set these yourself — they're present in the environment whenever your terraform is running inside a Massdriver deployment.

| Env var | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MASSDRIVER_DEPLOYMENT_ID` | yes | Identifies the deployment the terraform run belongs to. |
| `MASSDRIVER_TOKEN` | yes | Short-lived deployment secret. |

### Resolution order

When both sets of credentials are present, **deployment token auth wins** (the SDK assumes you're in a deployment context). Outside a deployment, the deployment env vars are absent, so the SDK falls through to API key auth.

## Which resources work with which credentials?

`massdriver_resource` is the only resource that **requires** deployment token auth — it's backed by a deployment-scoped REST endpoint and fast-fails outside a deployment. `massdriver_instance_alarm` is the only resource that accepts **either**, because its `instance_id` defaults from deployment env vars when present but can also be set explicitly when running from CI.

Every other resource is platform-scoped: deployment tokens don't carry the server-side permissions needed to create or modify them, so they require an API key.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) Massdriver API key — a service account token or a personal access token (`mds_` / `md_` prefix). Overrides `MASSDRIVER_API_KEY`. Keep this out of version control; prefer the env var or `TF_VAR_*` for production setups.
- `organization_id` (String) Massdriver organization ID this provider operates against. Overrides `MASSDRIVER_ORGANIZATION_ID`.
- `url` (String) Massdriver API base URL. Overrides `MASSDRIVER_URL`. Only set when targeting a self-hosted instance.
